was: Los Padres National Forest campground on Hwy 33 along the North Fork Matilija Creek; ~69 family sites (incl. some double sites), paved spurs, RVs to ~35 ft though some sites cap at 20-25 ft; no potable water or dump station. 59 sites reservable on recreation.gov, remainder FCFS. --Claude

was: BLM Barstow Field Office campground in Rainbow Basin Natural Area, ~8 mi N of Barstow. 22 sites (picnic table + fire ring), central potable-water tap, vault toilets, no hookups, no dump. Level pads fit small-to-mid RVs; reached by a few miles of maintained washboard gravel road (drive-in). $6/night, first-come, first-served. --Claude

was: Inyo County park on 80-acre Diaz Lake, 3 mi S of Lone Pine off US-395. ~100 lakeside sites (some with water hookups), accommodates 30 ft-plus RVs; reservable online plus FCFS sites; open year-round. --Claude

was: USFS campground along Lee Vining Creek in Lee Vining Canyon (Hwy 120, ~2 mi W of US-395) at ~7,300 ft. 51 non-hookup sites; vault toilets, no potable water, bear lockers. First-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov); RVs to ~40 ft. --Claude
note: USFS campground along Lee Vining Creek in Lee Vining Canyon (Hwy 120, ~2 mi W of US-395) at ~7,300 ft. 51 sites; bear lockers. --Claude

was: Small high-country USFS campground at the junction of Hwy 120 and Saddlebag Lake Rd near the Tioga Pass Yosemite entrance, ~9,500 ft. 13 sites, no hookups, no water (bring your own), vault toilets, FCFS (register on site). Sites 1-5 take RVs to 40 ft (25-ft RV limit on the bridge; a 23-ft rig fits); sites 6-13 cap at 18 ft and the road beyond site 5 is not recommended for trailers. --Claude

was: Wright's Beach Campground in Sonoma Coast State Park, on Hwy 1 N of Bodega Bay. 27 drive-in sites (paved spurs, table, fire ring) right on or steps from the beach; max trailer length 27 ft, no hookups/showers, flush toilets, no dump. Reservable via ReserveCalifornia (FCFS at kiosk within 48 hr). --Claude

was: RV camping at the Dixon May Fair fairgrounds (36th District Agricultural Association), open year-round to RVs/trailers subject to event scheduling; 14-day max stay. 20 gravel full-hookup sites (30/50A) plus 8 electric-only (20A) sites, dump station; first come, first served (the fair's rentals page, read 2026-10-12). --Claude

was: Operated by El Dorado Irrigation District on the west shore of Silver Lake at ~7,200 ft off Hwy 88 (Carson Pass). 42 sites, first-come, first-served (no reservations, unlike USFS Silver Lake East). Bear boxes, fire rings, pit toilets, no showers, no hookups. RV/trailer sites present. --Claude

was: USFS Tahoe National Forest (Truckee RD) campground on the Truckee River beside Hwy 89, ~1-3 mi south of Truckee. ~70 single/double sites, no hookups; vault toilets, drinking water. Most sites reservable online with a few kept FCFS. --Claude

was: PG&E-operated campground (utility-run = private per convention) on the south shore of Bucks Lake, 16731 Bucks Lake Rd, Quincy. 65 sites, no hookups, potable water, vault toilets, dump station; a few sites fit RVs up to 30 ft, most best for tents. Reservable through PG&E (2-night min); sites 10 and 14-29 are first-come, first-served. Open early June to early October. --Claude  Bucks Lake drawn down below normal after Labor Day 2026 for dam repairs; boat ramps unusable from about mid-September 2026 (PG&E notice, 2026-10-10). --Claude  Reservations need at least 2 nights; first-come, first-served sites can be taken for one night (PG&E, 2026-10-10). --Claude

RVs reservable; tents and small rigs (≤17 ft) sans service are first-come, first-served. --Claude

First-come, first-served (self-registration); open ~May 15-Oct 26. --Claude

was: Municipal dry campsite on the Cape Bonavista headland near the lighthouse, maintained by the Bonavista Recreation Committee. Self-contained RVs, campers and tents welcome; outhouses and picnic tables, no hookups. First-come, first-served, 3-night max, donations appreciated. Coastal hiking trails and whale/iceberg viewing. --Claude

was: Family-owned RV park at 900 Wood Ave W in Big Stone Gap, beside the South Fork Powell River and on the Greenbelt walking/bike trail into downtown. Operator's page: all sites full hookup with 30 and 50 amp, pull-thrus available, open year round; large pavilion, bathhouse, laundry, dump station, free wifi. Directory listings put the site count around 39. Rates by phone (276-523-0055 or toll-free 1-866-523-0055); no online booking. Do not confuse it with the mobile-home rows on Butterfly Lane immediately north across Wood Ave - those are a separate residential park. RV Life 5*/$$ ~$34/night (auto 9/2026). --Claude

was: Primitive open-meadow camping on the 1,800-acre Graves Mountain Farm & Lodges property in the Rose River valley, at the edge of Shenandoah National Park. Operator's campground page: 'RV - any size' welcome, pick-your-own spot across roughly 7 acres of meadow that expands to about 55 acres for holidays and festival weekends; no hookups; water spigots at the front of the campground, porta and pit toilets, showers at the farm's bathhouse behind the packing shed. Dump station $40 per use (Google review, confirmed in the owner's reply: the farm has no sewer, so the tank is pumped and hauled by truck). Rates are per person, under 5 free; horses $10 each and horse campers are assigned designated spots. Pay online or at the honor box. 7-day camping limit. Two mountain streams and two fishing ponds on the farm; restaurant in the Main Lodge. --Claude Corrected 2026-10-01 against the operator page (staff-collection and year-round claims removed); the $40 dump fee is sourced to a Google review and the owner's reply, found by AWH. --Claude

was: Wooded fishing camp on the Susquehanna at the mouth of the Juniata, just north of Duncannon and a short walk from the Appalachian Trail (the owners run an AT hiker shuttle). Operator's rates page lists full-hookup sites, water-and-electric sites, and no-hookup tent sites plus a separate off-river tent area; about 40 sites per the RV Life record. Operator's camping page: "Most of our sites are wooded, and over half are located along one of our two rivers," and the season is April 1 to December 1, "river permitting" - it sits on the floodplain, so late-season and high-water closures happen. Sites and interior lanes are wooded and unpaved off a grade crossing of the Norfolk Southern line, fine for a 23-ft rig but no big-rig suitability is claimed. Rates are not published online ("Please Call" on every line) and there is no online booking - reserve by phone or email; check-in 5 PM, check-out 4 PM, three-day minimum on holiday weekends. A Hipcamp listing exists but is still marked "coming soon," so it is not a live booking channel. Boat, canoe and kayak rental plus a bait shop on site. RV Life 4.5*/$$ ~$27/night (auto 9/2026). --Claude

was: Listed by RV Life as "Pine Creek Campground" at 3686 US-6; the operating name on its own Facebook page and in directory listings is Woodland's Campground on Pine Creek, 9 Woodlands Ln, Wellsboro (the Watrous hamlet between Gaines and Ansonia, Tioga County). About 35 sites on mowed grass loops between US-6 and Pine Creek, with full hookups including 50-amp, pull-through and back-in sites, dump station, restrooms and showers; tents accepted, no cabins. Walking distance to Pine Creek and the Pine Creek Rail Trail, and about 15 minutes from Colton Point / Leonard Harrison and the PA Grand Canyon. Satellite shows sheds or decks beside many of the trailers, so a good share of the pads are seasonal campers - call ahead for a transient site. No online booking channel found; reserve by phone. Caveat: the campground's official site (a Google Sites page) is behind a Google sign-in wall and is not publicly viewable, so the Facebook page is the live channel and no operator rates page could be read; rates below are the directory figure, not an operator quote. RV Life 5*/$$ ~$40/night (auto 9/2026). --Claude

was: 31 Ponderosa Dr, in the Bethany area northeast of Honesdale; under new ownership since 2020. The operator's site map shows roughly 85 numbered drive-in sites in four areas - Hillside H01-H27, Lakeside L01-L41, Kossack Court/Sabol Circle T01-T08 and Kasey Trail/Laurel Dr P01-P07 - plus seven cabins and two rustic tent sites, colour-coded seasonal versus non-seasonal with a solid block of non-seasonal sites in each loop. Its Firefly Reservations engine books nightly and asks for RV length, offering Lake Area, Lakefront, Deluxe Sewer and Rustic RV/Tent site classes; hookups run 15/20/30 amp with water, and sewer on the deluxe sites (no 50 amp advertised). Salt-water pool, mini golf, boat rentals on the campground's own Lake Ponderosa, country store and rec hall. Seasonal rentals are sold too but must be paid by check rather than online. Open season is roughly mid-April to late October per directory listings; the operator's own pages do not publish the dates. RV Life 4*/$$ ~$40/night (auto 9/2026). --Claude

was: Formerly Longview Campground, same property at 7570 Robinson Road at the base of Cove Mountain in the Tuscarora range. Operator's own campground map shows 88 numbered drive-in sites - 30-amp water/electric, 50-amp, sewer and frost-free sewer classes - plus lettered primitive tent sites, two playgrounds, pool, pavilion, camp store, laundry and dump station; directory listings put it at 87 sites (18 full hookup, 69 water/electric) taking rigs to 43 ft. Reservations by phone only, no online booking; open roughly May through October, with a Haunted Trail run in the fall. Caveat: the operator's site still carries a stale 2022-2024 winter-closure line and a 2023 copyright, but the park is demonstrably operating - a July 2025 RV Life review describes friendly staff, a clean park, camp store and firewood on site. RV Life 4*/$$ ~$38/night (auto 9/2026). --Claude

was: Large private resort 3 mi south of Hill City off US-16/385 on Rafter J-Bar Rd, backing onto Black Hills National Forest and the Mickelson Trail. 200 sites in six camping areas (Main, Base, Ranch, Lower Ranch, The Island, Line) plus a separate cabin camp: full hookups, 30/50 amp, pull-throughs and back-ins, concrete-pad deluxe patio sites, pool and hot tub, bathhouses and laundry, store and playground. $6 reservation fee, $20 to request a specific site. Online booking was refusing reservations in Sept 2026 ("please call us directly") - phone to book. Good Sam Park with a military discount. Priced above the sweep's usual private gate.

was: In-town campground one block north of Wall Drug at the north edge of Wall, the gateway town for Badlands NP and Buffalo Gap National Grassland. 59 pull-thru RV sites in rows A-G, all with water and 30/20 or 50/30/20 amp electric; many add sewer and/or cable; sites 9-10B are the ones recommended for high-profile big rigs. Separate tent sites. Showers, laundry, dog park, campground-wide wifi; the swimming pool is GONE - guests use the City of Wall pool. Open May 1 - Oct 15, 10% veteran and active-military discount, check-in 1pm and check-out 11am MST, 7-day cancellation. Priced above the sweep's usual private gate.

was: KOA Holiday on the south bank of the White River on SD-44, about 4 mi south of Interior and the Badlands NP south entrance. Roughly 139 sites among planted shade trees - full hookups with 20/30 amp and cable, tent sites and camper cabins - plus pool, mini golf, bike rentals, store, laundry and showers. Season runs late April to mid-October. Phone number deliberately omitted: the only one published in the directories is KOA's central reservations line, not the campground's. Priced above the sweep's usual private gate.

was: Hotel plus campground on SD-377 at the edge of Interior, a mile from the Badlands NP entrance - the closest full-service base to the park's south side. About 80 level gravel pull-through sites with full hookups at 50/30 amp (plus 30-amp full-hookup and primitive/tent options) among roughly 100 total; two bathhouses, guest laundry, restaurant, store, pool and free wifi. Open May through September. Formerly Badlands Interior Motel & Campground. Priced above the sweep's usual private gate.

was: Five RV sites on a family cow-calf ranch off US-14 six miles east of Wall, at the north end of the 56-acre Tennyson Dam reservoir. Four sites have full hookups and one is water and electric; grass between sites, horse corrals, a grain-bin gazebo with a propane fire pit, and a two-bedroom cabin built from two joined grain bins. Fishing pier, kayaks and a paddle boat available on request. Open May 15 to Oct 30. Small and thinly reviewed, so the details here come from the operator's own page rather than aggregators. Priced above the sweep's usual private gate.

was: Veteran-owned, Native-American-run campground on a ranch near the ghost town of Scenic, between the Badlands and the Black Hills. About 15 spacious pull-through RV sites with water and electric (amperage not published on the operator's page), picnic tables and fire rings, a dump station and a new shower house; cabins and primitive tent sites too, plus a saloon, shooting range and guided hunts on the property. Side-by-side and ATV friendly. Good Sam Park with a military discount. Priced above the sweep's usual private gate.
note: Veteran-owned, Native-American-run campground on a ranch near the ghost town of Scenic, between the Badlands and the Black Hills. About 15 spacious pull-through RV sites with water and electric (amperage not published on the operator's page), picnic tables and fire rings, a new shower house; cabins and primitive tent sites too, plus a saloon, shooting range and guided hunts on the property. Side-by-side and ATV friendly.

was: The big destination resort 5 mi west of Mount Rushmore on SD-244, KOA-branded and lodge-attached. Around 500 sites: deluxe patio sites with 50-amp, full hookups and cable, plus full-hookup and water/electric RV sites, tent sites and a large cabin/lodge operation. Five comfort stations, three laundries, camping kitchen, pools, dining, shopping and a rodeo on the property. Busy, resort-priced and the most convenient base for Rushmore itself. Priced above the sweep's usual private gate.

was: In-town KOA on E SD-44 on the east side of Rapid City, about 228 sites with pull-through full hookups at 50/30/20 amp plus cable, a pool and the usual KOA store and laundry. Open year round, which is unusual in the Black Hills and makes it the shoulder-season option. Priced above the sweep's usual private gate.

was: Open-prairie RV resort on SD-79 south of Hermosa, between Rapid City and Hot Springs and handy for Custer State Park's east side. About 150 full-hookup sites in long angled pull-through rows, plus cabins and tent sites, an event centre, dog yard, laundry and showers. Monthly stays are offered alongside nightly, but short-term booking is the front door. Now run as part of the Streamside RV Resorts group. Priced above the sweep's usual private gate.

was: 100 sites in the pines on the Norbeck Byway a mile north of Custer, close to Crazy Horse, Sylvan Lake, the Needles and Jewel Cave. Full-hookup 50-amp pull-throughs and 30/50-amp back-ins with free cable, water-and-electric sites, and rustic and group sites; tipis and cabins too. Open May 1 to October 15. Priced above the sweep's usual private gate.

was: Quiet, wooded campground off US-16 west of Custer, set back from highway noise under tall ponderosa. 50- and 30-amp full-hookup sites, water-and-electric, primitive and tent sites, camper cabins and a retro trailer rental; two bath houses, laundry, game room, RV supplies, free wifi. Open May to October, with a two-night deposit required over the Sturgis Rally dates. Priced above the sweep's usual private gate.

was: Family-run for 40-plus years on the north edge of Spearfish, handy to I-90 and Spearfish Canyon. About 228 sites from deluxe pull-thru full hookups to shaded tent sites and primitive camping cabins, with three heated pools, two laundromats, rec room, playground, basketball court, dump station and site fire pits; a small animal farm for the kids. Good Sam Park with a military discount. Priced above the sweep's usual private gate.
